title: The Rule of 72: Double Your Money Math In Your Head
golden_rule: Divide 72 by the annual rate to estimate years to double.
description: The Rule of 72 is a mental shortcut that estimates how long money takes to double at a given annual growth rate. Divide 72 by the rate, and you get the approximate number of years. This video explains the maths in plain language with one simple example, so you can sanity-check any growth number in seconds. It is educational content only, not investment advice, and all rates shown are illustrative assumptions. Watch the full video for more beginner money basics.

beats.vo: How long does money take to double? You can work it out in four seconds.

spec.headline: Doubling money, done in your head
spec.sub: One number does all the work

beats.vo: The trick is one number. Seventy-two.
Take the yearly growth rate. Divide seventy-two by it. That answer is roughly the years to double.
Say something grew at twelve percent a year. Seventy-two divided by twelve. Six years.
Now flip the rate. At six percent a year, the same money takes twelve years. Half the rate, double the wait.
It works on the other side too. If prices rise at six percent, your costs double in about twelve years.
So remember. Seventy-two divided by the rate equals years to double. Full video has more.
